text.p01: To everyone tying knots, one loop at a time: take your time, then finish. A story about doing things well and getting them done.
text.p03: In the misty green mountains by the sea lived Zayn, a little weaver bird with bright yellow feathers and the fastest beak around.
text.p04: Weaver birds weave their homes from grass, knot by knot. But Zayn never waited. Zip, zip, done! He was always finished first.
text.p05: "The big wind is coming," said the weavers. "Every nest must be ready!" Zayn needed a nest for himself and his little sister, Rima.
text.p06: Zip, zip, done! By lunchtime, his nest was hanging from the branch. Hana the chameleon peered at it. "Is it done, or done well?"
text.p07: Zayn just laughed. But that evening, the first misty drizzle came. His nest sagged. Bits of grass popped out, and a hole opened.
text.p08: Zayn stuffed in a little grass. "Good enough!" he chirped. Rima peeked out through the hole and blinked. "Are you sure?"
text.p09: The next day, a gusty wind blew up the valley. The nest swung, and wobbled, and slipped, and splash! It fell into the pool below.
text.p10: Zayn and Rima were safe on the branch, but their home was gone. Zayn's feathers drooped. Fast wasn't the same as good.
text.p11: Hana stepped slowly along the branch. She gripped, she tested, and only then did she step. Grip, test, step. Nothing ever slipped.
text.p12: Zayn took a breath. "This time," he said, "I'll do it well." He chose strong green grass and tied his first knot. Loop, pull, tug!
text.p13: Loop, pull, tug! Each knot was tight and strong. Weaving slowly felt different, like humming a song instead of shouting it.
text.p14: Then Zayn spotted a crooked knot. He untied it and tied it again. Then another. And another. "It has to be perfect," he muttered.
text.p15: Days went by. Zayn tied and untied, tied and untied. The other weavers were finished, but Zayn's nest was still only half a nest.
text.p16: Rima waited under a leaf, shivering a little in the mist. Over the sea, big gray clouds were rolling in. The big wind was coming.
text.p17: "My knots aren't perfect!" cried Zayn. Hana tested a twig, then stepped onto it. "If I waited for a perfect branch, I'd never get anywhere."
text.p18: Zayn looked at his nest. It was strong and snug, with a few crooked knots. "It's good," he said. "Now let's finish it!"
text.p19: Loop, pull, tug! He wove the round roof. Loop, pull, tug! He wove the little doorway. Then Zayn tied the very last knot.
text.p20: "Loop, pull, tug… and done!" he sang, just as the first big gust came rushing up the valley. "Rima, come inside!" Whoosh! In she zoomed.
text.p21: All night the big wind blew. Branches swayed and leaves flew. Zayn's nest swung back and forth, back and forth, but every knot held tight.
text.p22: Inside, Zayn and Rima were warm and dry. Rima snuggled close. "Our nest is just right," she whispered, "crooked knots and all."
text.p23: When the wind was gone, the young weavers asked Zayn to teach them. "Loop, pull, tug," he showed them. "Do your best… and then finish!"
text.p24: Loop, pull, tug… and done! Not too fast, not too slow. Do it well, and get it done. The End
text.cover: Knot by Knot. A Story About Doing Things Well and Getting Them Done
